purpose: Three lighting-direction paintovers, each courtyard above and morgue below. Concepts for review, not in-engine screenshots.

variants.name: clear-day
variants.prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather. Create a faithful LIGHTING PAINTOVER for a stylized 3D game's art-direction review.
INPUT ROLE: the supplied image is the edit target, a FOUR-panel comparison. Use ONLY its TWO LEFT PANELS: upper-left is the original cemetery courtyard; lower-left is the original morgue interior. Ignore BOTH RIGHT PANELS, which are rejected old paintovers. Remove all comparison headers and corner labels.
OUTPUT: ONE high-resolution portrait 4:5 image containing EXACTLY TWO equal landscape panels stacked vertically: courtyard on top, morgue interior below, separated by a very thin dark line. Each panel must retain the ENTIRE original left-panel camera framing and perspective, with no scene cropping. No new typography or variant titles; preserve only the existing diegetic signs.
CRITICAL INVARIANTS: preserve the original geometry, camera, perspective, object count and arrangement, the long low wooden morgue, plum shingle roof, crooked hilltop chapel, paths, grave plots, fence and twisted tree. Interior must retain identical beams, windows, doors, registry counter on left, dressing table mid-background, rack, back-right stockroom counter and large foreground table on right. Do not add people, props, extra windows, lamps, foliage, architecture, roof holes or scenery. This is the same modest low-poly game render with lighting changed, not a redesigned richly detailed illustration. Preserve material identity and the existing hand-painted procedural texture character.
ART QUALITY: coherent light direction; large composed light/shadow masses; nuanced reflected light; surfaces and furniture feel grounded; playable/readable darks; a few deliberate highlights. Interior focal attention should land on existing work surfaces rather than empty floor. Keep the ceiling readable but subdued. Doorways remain ordinary openings with depth; never luminous screens. Small pane glass may be bright with dark frames and a tonal gradient, never solid white rectangles. Lit wood still looks like wood.
ABSOLUTE AVOIDS: no visible volumetric shafts, cones, rectangles or portals, no god rays, no added lens flare, no fog inside the room, no strong vignette, no bloom wash, no solid-black crushed shadows. Do not imitate the rejected right-hand paintovers.
VARIANT A — CLEAR STORYBOOK DAY.
Exterior: clean cobalt-to-pale-blue daylight sky, warm-neutral mid-afternoon sunlight from upper right, lively emerald and sage grass, restrained golden straw paths, original aubergine roof. Elegant soft-edged directional shadows in muted lavender/slate, subtle green reflected light near grass. A broad broken shadow across part of the foreground, an inviting sunlit middle ground. Distant hills lower contrast. Fresh, clear, cheerful but still delightfully odd gothic game; absolutely avoid yellow-green exposure wash. Make the building's eaves and doorway depth tangible.
Interior: broad cool-neutral blue skylight through existing openings establishes soft volume, mixed with restrained honey light from the EXISTING pendant lamps focused on counters/table tops. Deep aubergine-brown ceiling beams, natural walnut timber, soft contact shading. Daylight remains dominant, lamp accents small. Mostly broad diffuse illumination with at most one restrained soft sun patch on an existing work surface; no multiple patterned floor patches. The mood is airy, welcoming, tactile, quietly magical, not a dark horror room.

VARIANT B — COPPER EVENING / ROSE AND VIOLET.
Exterior: distinctly late golden hour, low peach-copper sun from the right grazing the front wall and grass edges. Pale apricot near horizon transitioning to dusty rose and muted lavender-blue sky above, retaining the original sky shapes. Deep but readable cool plum shadows and mossy green grass; sunlit roof catches subtle copper-red highlights while staying recognizably plum. Broad long coherent shadows. Entrance is inviting because of a small amber practical accent and visible warm interior, not a glowing opening. Preserve neutral areas so the whole image is NOT orange, brown or sepia. Refined complementary color harmony and gently theatrical atmosphere.
Interior: much stronger warm/cool separation than A: concentrated amber light from EXISTING pendants on registry and preparation surfaces, rose dusk skylight entering the existing windows, muted violet fill in recesses. The focal work surfaces feel lit and alive against a quieter room; rich tobacco and oxblood wood retain color distinctions. A restrained low oblique sunlight accent can graze an existing beam or tabletop, but NOT repeated glowing rectangles on the floor. Keep all doors visibly ordinary wood/openings and all three functional zones readable. Warm evening sanctuary in a strange cemetery, not smoky tavern, not orange wash.

VARIANT C — SILVER OVERCAST / COOL FAIRYTALE.

Grass remains richly differentiated jade and sage, paths pale natural ochre, timber soft walnut, roof dark blackberry. Soft occlusion and reflected skylight create sculptural volume without hard sunlight patches. Reduce distant contrast for depth while keeping foreground color and edge definition. No rain, no wet surfaces, no added weather objects. Small existing lanterns and windows supply sparse honey accents. This must be beautiful, fresh, atmospheric and playable rather than desaturated, grim or murky.
Interior: the brightest and softest WINDOW skylight of the three options; cool pearl / pale cyan illumination rolls broadly across tables and walls, with dusky teal-violet recesses and distinctly warm tiny EXISTING pendants. Surfaces near windows are softly brighter with natural falloff. No hard cast window rectangles and absolutely no visible shafts. Warm lamp pools are intimate small accents; avoid an overall orange interior. Preserve walnut wood texture rather than making it blue-painted. Quiet, mysterious, delicate, luminous, strong tactile contact shadows but no black crush. The registry and preparation table are clearly legible as focal stations.
